# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 50 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_050_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 1 — You Are a Stranger in This City

**50:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a resident alien — a foreigner — and that your real home city is far away. If you already know the city where you're actually going to live permanently, why are you investing in fields, expensive furniture, fancy buildings, and unnecessary rooms here? Anyone who makes those kinds of preparations in this city can't get back to their own city.

**50:2** You foolish, double-minded, miserable person — can't you see that all these things belong to someone else and fall under someone else's authority? The lord of this city is going to say to you: I don't want you living in my city. Get out — because you haven't been following my laws. So when he throws you out — you with all your fields and houses and piles of possessions — what are you going to do with all of it?

**50:3** The lord of this place has every right to say to you: obey my laws or leave my territory. Then what will you do? You already have a law from your own city. Are you going to throw away your own law completely — giving up everything — just to live by the laws of this place? Be careful. That might cost you more than you think. If you want to go back to your own city eventually, you won't be welcome there, because you abandoned its law. You'll be locked out.

**50:4** Here's what to do instead: as a foreigner living in someone else's land, keep your needs simple — just enough for daily necessities. Stay ready. That way, when the master of this city tries to expel you for not following his laws, you can leave his city freely, go home to your own city, and live joyfully under your own law without any harm done.

**50:5** So pay attention, you who serve God and carry him in your hearts. Do the works of God. Remember his commandments and the promises he has made. Trust him to follow through on them when you keep his commandments. Instead of buying fields here, invest in people who are suffering — as much as each person is able. Visit widows and orphans. Don't neglect them. Spend your wealth and possessions on the kinds of fields and houses you'll receive from God.

**50:6** That's exactly why the Master made you wealthy — so you could do this kind of work for him. It's far better to acquire the kind of fields, goods, and houses that will be waiting for you in your own city when you arrive there. That's a truly noble and sacred investment — no grief, no fear, only joy. Don't invest the way the pagans do. That approach is worthless for people who serve God.

**50:7** Make the investments that bring you real joy. Don't try to claim what belongs to someone else, don't touch it, don't even crave it — coveting someone else's possessions is evil. Do your own work, and you will be saved."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the Two Cities allegory's challenge to Christian wealth and material investment.*
